scenarios.title: A stranger arrives
scenarios.goal: You are visiting this house for the first time; the companion has never met you. Come in, say hello, chat casually about your day, and ask the companion a question or two about itself or the house. Don't give your name unless the companion asks for it.

people.name: Chris
people.about: A friendly man in his thirties, a friend of the family dropping by. Relaxed, a bit chatty.

scenarios.title: Introduces themself, then comes back
scenarios.goal: Introduce yourself to the companion by name (you are Maya, you have just moved into the house) and chat for a moment. After the break you come back into the room: without giving your name again, check whether the companion remembers who you are, for example by asking if it remembers you or what your name is.

people.name: Maya
people.about: A cheerful woman in her late twenties who just moved in. Warm and direct.

breaks.note: You left the room for a while and are now coming back in.

scenarios.title: Two people in the room
scenarios.goal: Alex and Rose are both in the living room with the companion. Alex asks something about the household (for example when dinner is, or where the spare blanket went) and Rose answers it, sometimes before the companion does. Let the conversation go back and forth between the two of them and the companion; each line is spoken by exactly one of them.

people.name: Alex
people.about: A man in his forties, Rose's son, practical and a little forgetful.

people.name: Rose
people.about: Alex's mother, in her seventies, gentle and knows where everything in the house is.

scenarios.title: A curious child
scenarios.goal: You are a curious seven-year-old who lives here. Ask the companion curious questions, one at a time, like why the sky is blue or whether fish sleep, and react to its answers like a child would. Use short sentences and simple words.

people.name: Lily
people.about: A seven-year-old girl, excited and giggly, who asks 'why' about everything.

scenarios.title: Cuts in while the companion answers
scenarios.goal: Ask the companion something that takes a longer answer, such as how to make pancakes or what to do on a rainy afternoon. On the turn you cut in, you change your mind or ask something else while the companion is still answering, the way people do.

people.name: Sam
people.about: A cheerful young man, a bit impatient, who thinks out loud.
